chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Kukabi, from al-Umari al-Bufi, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who made a vow to God in something permissible (non-disobedience), what is upon him if he does not fulfill his vow? He said: He frees a slave, or gives charity, or fasts for two consecutive months.

key_terms.غَيْرِ مَعْصِيَةٍ: in a permissible matter (not in disobedience)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for breaking a vow to God?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Isfahani's chain within al-Istibsar, this hadith from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) clarifies that vows made in permissible matters (ghayr ma'siyyah) require expiation if broken, mirroring the structure of kaffarat al-yamin. The sequence of freeing a slave, feeding the poor, or fasting two consecutive months reflects the classical juristic consensus on fulfilling religious commitments with sincerity. This ruling underscores the binding nature of personal vows in Shia fiqh, treating them as self-imposed obligations akin to oaths.
